items.entity: Configuration-1 load on the free face (the face opposite the clamped face)
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says the loads are 'applied to the side opposite to a fixed one (Fig.1(A, D))'. Where configuration 1's load sits on that face is shown only in its BVP sketch (Fig. 2(A) according to the captions), which I can't see. The Fig. 3 caption ('xz cross section passing through symmetry plane', Example 1) suggests the load lies on the mid-width line of the free face. Coordinates below assume the clamp at x=0, the loaded face at x=1, y = width, z = height.
readings: Centre of the face: y=0.5, z=0.5 (symmetric about two planes)
Midpoint of the bottom edge: y=0.5, z=0 (the top edge, z=1, gives a mirror-image layout)
Line across the full width at mid-height: z=0.5, y from 0 to 1
Line along the full bottom edge: z=0, y from 0 to 1
Spread over the whole free face
A corner of the face, y=0, z=0 (only if config 1 is the non-symmetric case and 'symmetry plane' in Fig. 3 just means the cube's mid-plane)

items.description: The text never states a load direction; it appears only in the BVP figure I can't see. The title 'Cantilever supports', the phrase 'standard example' and the agreement with earlier cantilever results [23,24,4] point to a transverse (bending) load. The xz symmetry plane in Fig. 3 suggests the cantilever axis and the load lie in the xz plane. The sign of the load doesn't matter for single-load compliance.
readings: Transverse, inside the xz symmetry plane (e.g. -z, perpendicular to the cantilever axis x)
Transverse, normal to the symmetry plane (+/-y): the same as the first reading up to a rotation if the load is centred, different if it sits on an edge
Axial, normal to the loaded face (tension or compression along x), as in the uniform-tension cube of the literally cited Fig. 1(A)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 never says whether the load is a concentrated force, a traction on a patch, a line load or a traction over the whole face. Sec. 4.3 and Sec. 5 describe Sec. 4.1 as 'mixed BVPs' and keep 'concentrated force loadings' for Sec. 4.2, which weakly hints at a distributed load. Also, the BEM tractions are constant per triangle, so even a 'point' load must cover some patch of voxel faces of unstated size.
readings: Concentrated force at a single grid node
Uniform traction on one voxel face (1/64 x 1/64)
Uniform traction on a small square patch (2x2 to 8x8 voxel faces, side 1/32 to 1/8)
Line load one voxel row wide across the full width of the face
Uniform traction over the entire free face

items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives no force or traction value. Results appear only as the normalized Psi/Psi0 (Fig. 2(F)), and the relative threshold makes the layout independent of the load magnitude.
readings: Total force |F| = 1
Traction |t| = 1 on the loaded area (so total force = loaded area)
Any other value (only scales Psi)

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'the symmetric configuration appears significantly stiffer than the non-symmetric one' but never says which of the two is configuration 1. The Fig. 3 caption also calls the cut a 'symmetry plane' for both Example 1 and Example 2. That conflicts with one case being 'non-symmetric', unless it only means that case has one symmetry plane fewer.
readings: Configuration 1 is the symmetric case (e.g. load centred on the free face; the stiffer curve in Fig. 2(F))
Configuration 1 is the non-symmetric case (e.g. load at the bottom edge or a corner of the free face; the more compliant curve)

items.entity: Figure cross-references for the configuration-1 BVP
items.description: Sec. 4.1 cites 'Fig.1(A, D)' for the initial BVPs, and Fig. 1(B,E), 1(C), 1(F) and Fig. 2(A,B) for results. By the captions, these are actually Fig. 2(A-F) and Fig. 3. The cited Fig. 1(A) is the Sec. 3 benchmark cube 'subjected to a uniform tension' (N=2), and Fig. 1(D) is a timing plot.
readings: The intended reference is Fig. 2(A), the cantilever BVP I can't see, so the load stays undetermined
Taken literally, Fig. 1(A): uniform normal tension over the face opposite the clamped face

items.description: Sec. 4.1 and the Fig. 2 caption give alpha_c = 0.6, but in Algorithm 1 alpha_c is only a stopping test ('if alpha < alpha_c then break') applied after each hard-kill removal step. The run stopped after 3 iterations at some unreported alpha below 0.6, and with so few, large removal steps the gap may be noticeable.
readings: Exactly 0.60 (as a volume constraint)
The unreported final hard-kill value below 0.6, e.g. about 0.55-0.59

items.description: Sec. 2.3 gives only 'Typically, C=0.001÷0.1', and Sec. 4.1 never states the value used. The paper says C sets the level of detail and acts as an implicit regularization (Sec. 2.3), and that the result 'strongly depends' on it (Sec. 5). The only clue is that alpha < 0.6 was reached after three iterations. Because D^T_max is driven by stress concentrations at the load and the clamp edges, how much material a given C removes also depends on how the load is discretized.
readings: Whatever C brings alpha below 0.6 in exactly 3 iterations

items.entity: Filter / regularization radius for a density-based re-run
items.description: The paper uses no explicit filter (Sec. 5: 'absence of explicit regularization'); regularization comes only implicitly from C and the voxel post-processing. So no filter radius or length scale is given to carry over to a structured-grid FE solver, which normally needs one to suppress checkerboards.
readings: No filter (binary thresholding only)
Sensitivity or density filter with radius about 1.5 voxels (about 0.023)
Filter radius 2-3 voxels (about 0.03-0.05)

items.description: Sec. 2.3 mentions a 'post-processing procedure excluding isolated voxels and surface irregularities' but doesn't define its rules (neighbourhood, connectivity criterion, what counts as an irregularity). It still changes the design passed to the next iteration. The Laplacian smoothing in Fig. 2(C) is a separate, display-only step.
readings: Remove only voxels with no face-adjacent solid neighbour
Also remove solid clusters not connected to the clamped face
Morphological opening/closing to remove one-voxel bumps and pits
No post-processing

items.entity: Voxels under the load and at the clamped face
items.description: Sec. 4.1 mentions no non-design regions, and Algorithm 1 voids any voxel below the threshold. It doesn't say whether the loaded voxels, or a layer of voxels at the clamped face, are protected from removal.
readings: No passive regions (every voxel can be removed)
Loaded voxel(s) or patch kept solid
A one-voxel layer on the clamped face kept solid
Both the loaded voxels and the clamped layer kept solid
